target_customer: Data center builders, operators and infrastructure equipment manufacturers
problem: AI data centers need skilled technicians to assemble, commission and maintain equipment, and the physical labor is scarce and slow to scale.
business_model: Robots deployed as technicians for data center operators; pricing model not stated, initial deployments targeted for early 2027
product_category: General purpose robot technicians, robotics and AI infrastructure

founders.name: Sergio Charles
education: Stanford, B.S. Mathematics & Computer Science and M.S. Statistics
founders.background_notes: YC page cites robotics research with Chelsea Finn and computer vision research with Andrew Ng. The brothers are described as co-founders.

founders.name: Luigi Charles
previous_startups: Sphere (fintech payments, founded and scaled; exit not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says Sphere grew to billions in transaction volume.

competitors.name: Boost Robotics
competitors.what: Autonomous mobile manipulation robots that inspect and interact with data center infrastructure
competitors.traction_then: YC Spring 2025 company; traction not verified

technical_complexity.rationale: General purpose manipulation that learns tasks from demonstrations and must work reliably around dense server hardware is research grade, and it needs custom robot hardware and real world deployment data.

defensibility.rationale: Demonstration and deployment data and hardware know-how compound over time, but the work is capital hungry and other funded teams chase the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large player built a data center technician robot as of the sources, and none acquired Darwin; other startups entered later.

market_need_then: AI data center buildout in 2025 created a shortage of skilled technicians and commissioning labor, and the founders pitch automating assembly, commissioning and maintenance.

identity.voice_and_tone: Robot technicians that assemble and maintain the machines civilization runs on

branding.community_and_virality: Pre-seed announced on X and covered by a few outlets; no evidence of merch or community.

brand_strength.rationale: Name echoes evolution and adaptation but is shared with other robotics projects such as DARwIn-OP and another YC backed Darwin, with no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Darwin Robotics is active and very early. Two brothers with Stanford AI research and a payments startup background joined YC in Fall 2025 and raised a 3.6M dollar pre-seed led by Link Ventures in November 2026, with deployments targeted for early 2027. Coverage notes no completed deployment yet, and later entrants such as Exclaim Robotics, which emerged from stealth in August 2026, show growing competition.
notes: Amount of 3.6M is stated by RuntimeWire (paywalled preview), Signalbase and the company's X thread as reported; one deal tracker shows 4M, so the 3.6M figure is used. Traded.co page returned 403. Investor list combines the company site backer list with press mentions; Globivest and Script Capital come only from the company site. Exclaim Robotics (August 2026) and Watney Robotics entered later and are not counted as competition at founding. Another YC backed company named Darwin makes humanoids and is a different firm.
